html:
The peace treaty that ended the First Opium War, signed on a British warship at Nanjing in August 1842. It was the first of the treaties the Chinese call the unequal treaties.

Britain had won the war with steamships and modern guns. Under the treaty the Qing:

  • gave Hong Kong Island to Britain;
  • opened five ports to British trade and residence: Canton, Amoy, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai;
  • paid 21 million silver dollars;
  • ended the Canton System and the monopoly of its licensed merchants;
  • agreed to fixed, low tariffs.

A follow-up treaty in 1843 let British subjects be tried under their own law and promised Britain any rights given to other powers. The United States and France soon got similar treaties.

The treaty did not even mention opium, which kept flowing in. It marks the start of what China calls its century of humiliation. Hong Kong and Shanghai grew into great trading cities.
